result: accepted: the owner's exact verdict approves building the measured public-preview mode and binds all four definitions

definitions.question: What is the mode called wherever the product names it?
definitions.proposed: “Public preview”, with “signed out” stated beside it wherever the mode is named — the profile selector, the window title, and the workbench header all read “Public preview — signed out”. It is never presented as the authenticated workbench with fields missing.
definitions.bound: “Public preview”, with “signed out” stated beside it wherever the mode is named — the profile selector, the window title, and the workbench header all read “Public preview — signed out”. It is never presented as the authenticated workbench with fields missing.

definitions.question: How are the shared hourly budget, and the things the preview cannot do, presented?
definitions.proposed: Not a persistent bar. A small ring indicator in the workbench fills as the shared hourly core budget is consumed, in the manner of Claude Desktop’s usage ring. Hovering it shows a tooltip carrying the consumed fraction and the reset time — “32% of the hourly limit · Resets in 3 hr 4 min” — and, in that same tooltip, what the preview cannot do: GitHub.com only, no review threads, no triage or publishing. A conditional request answered 304 spends one unit like any other, so the ring moves on refresh. Budget exhaustion is a typed refusal naming the limit and the reset time, never a network or authentication error.

definitions.question: How does the preview hand off to signing in?
definitions.proposed: The RFC-BPR-0016 device authorization flow is offered from the ring’s tooltip and from every refusal — budget exhausted, review threads unavailable, and any triage or publishing attempt — and returns to the same pull request after sign-in.
definitions.bound: The RFC-BPR-0016 device authorization flow is offered from the ring’s tooltip and from every refusal — budget exhausted, review threads unavailable, and any triage or publishing attempt — and returns to the same pull request after sign-in.

definitions.question: Which platforms and profiles does the preview support?
definitions.proposed: All three desktop platforms — macOS, Linux, and Windows x64 — because the preview needs no credential store. GitHub.com public repositories only; every GHES profile stays unavailable and sends zero requests. The sign-in handoff is shown only where device authorization is enabled on that platform: macOS and Linux today, since BPR-0310 is terminal, and Windows once BPR-0311 — now ready on the Windows lane — is terminal too.
